title: Raw rational descent of normalized integral pullback comparisons
statement: Given scalar realization data and actual normalized integral pullback arrows as in [def-weil-pbc-realization-pull-data], and completed composition and continuous identity comparisons satisfying the integral alpha composition and identity equations, extend the ordinary and completed integral restrictions to the raw scalar localizations. There exist the rational alpha, unit, completed compositor and identity isomorphisms. Their components on integral objects are the localized integral maps, they retain every uniformizer denominator, and rational alpha satisfies the specified identity and composition equations on every raw rational object.

proof.text: The tensor extension of an A-linear functor preserves pure tensors and composition. Extend natural isomorphisms by applying the scalar localization functor to their components. Tensor induction proves the compositor and identity comparisons, and linearity gives the unchanged-denominator formula.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; rationalization and inheritance of coherence

proof.text: The tensor Hom equivalence with triangulated rationalization makes the integral rationalization functor a localization at scalar isogenies. Its restriction on functor categories is fully faithful. Conjugate integral alpha by the realization integral isomorphisms, then lift through that restriction. The normalization is the map-preimage equation. Here the tensor Hom equivalence is the already proved Rationalization.tensorHomEquiv in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Complete.RationalizationHom; no new rationalization property is assumed.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; rationalization and inheritance of coherence

proof.text: Every raw object is an unchanged integral object. Write rational alpha as the conjugate of integral alpha. In its composition equation, cancel the adjacent scalar integral inverse and forward isomorphisms; naturality of the scalar integral comparison and rational compositor leaves the given integral equation. For identity use the integral completion unit inverse followed by ordinary identity, and cancel the unit.

theorem realizationPullRationalDescent
    (hc : realizationPullLawAlphaComp scalar arrow rationalComp completedComp)
    (hi : realizationPullLawAlphaId scalar arrow continuousId) :
    ∃ rationalAlpha : (∀ {T U : RealizationPullScheme l k} (h : RealizationPullHom T U),
      (arrow h).rationalCompleted ⋙ realizationPullRationalScalar l E (scalar T) ≅
        realizationPullRationalScalar l E (scalar U) ⋙ (arrow h).continuousPull),
      realizationPullLawRationalAlphaIntegral scalar arrow rationalAlpha ∧
      realizationPullLawRawFractions scalar arrow ∧
    ∃ rawUnit : (∀ {T U : RealizationPullScheme l k} (h : RealizationPullHom T U),
      (arrow h).rationalOrdinary ≅ (arrow h).rationalCompleted),
      realizationPullLawRawUnitIntegral scalar arrow rawUnit ∧
    ∃ rawComp : (∀ {T U V : RealizationPullScheme l k}
      (h : RealizationPullHom T U) (j : RealizationPullHom U V),
      (arrow j).rationalCompleted ⋙ (arrow h).rationalCompleted ≅
        (arrow (h ≫ j)).rationalCompleted),
      realizationPullLawRawCompIntegral scalar arrow completedComp rawComp ∧
    ∃ rawId : (∀ T : RealizationPullScheme l k,
      (arrow (𝟙 (Over.mk (T.scheme ↘ Spec (.of k))))).rationalCompleted ≅ 𝟭 _),
      realizationPullLawRawIdIntegral scalar arrow rawId ∧
      realizationPullLawRawAlphaComp scalar arrow rationalAlpha rationalComp rawComp ∧
      realizationPullLawRawAlphaId scalar arrow rationalAlpha continuousId rawId
